items.signal_prefix: Capacity sold out (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: 'We are mo

set.signal: Capacity sold out (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: 'We are more or less sold out for 26, 27'; delivery times being discussed today are 2029 and 2030, customers with many projects are talking about 2030 and 2031, and the project announced that morning (the 1.1 GW order) has delivery until 2031. Martin Widner (head of global sales for data centers and power solutions): 'the slot reservation reaches out now till 2030'; '2027 is completely sold out, so there are no further slots to be freed up for 2027', with slots now being freed for 2028 and, with the further Waukesha ramp-up, 2029 and 2030; 'We still have many requests for projects which we are not able to fulfill because of capacity'; 'capacity constraint, but not market constraint.' CFO Dennis Schulze: demand 'has recently been exceeding our ability to take orders'; INNIO is deliberately not selling the whole planned capacity curve yet and frees up slots over time as the ramp-up proves on time and in spec.

items.reason: The CEO said the project announced that morning (press release) delivers till 2031; it was not announced on the call.
items.evidence: the project what we announced this morning, is delivery till 2031

items.signal_prefix: Large orders (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: the Q2 highligh

set.signal: Large orders (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: the Q2 highlight was a 1.1 GW order from a megascale data center customer (not named), one of the largest orders in INNIO's history, with more than 200 Jenbacher J624 engines expected to provide behind-the-meter prime power and delivery until 2031. Martin Widner: the order is 'even below 30%' of the quarter's data center order intake; part of it is containerized (more scope) and part is for a powerhouse installation (less scope). CFO Dennis Schulze: 'Size of 1.1 GW is not the exception, it's now, I would say, common.' CEO: 'we announced the Greco [as transcribed] one was 1.25 GW. It's a little bit longer run project'; 'we are working with Greco, a long-term contract delivering engines Type four, Type six. There are many of these coming up.'

items.reason: The call never names Aggreko; linking Greco to Aggreko is an inference the source does not state.

items.signal_prefix: Demand and customers (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: 'There

set.signal: Demand and customers (management): CEO Olaf Berlien: 'There is no decline or weaknesses in the pipeline', strength is expected in H2, and additional customers are entering the top customer profile; of the 'six or seven big hyperscalers, they are all our customers'; 'we do not have one single cancellation today in smaller project as well as in big projects', citing diligence on project financing and customers. Martin Widner: demand for INNIO's product 'is as high as ever', with projects in 2029, 2030 and 2031 and a pipeline developed with Energy-as-a-Service and rental companies for different hyperscalers 'going into permits already into plans for 2031, 2032'; customer projects are on time with no big construction or permitting delays so far; the containerized solution needs little on-site EPC capability, an advantage while U.S. EPC capacity is constrained. CEO: behind-the-meter solutions 'are not the bridge solution, but are here to stay' (citing a BloombergNEF analysis that gas engines can offer the lowest levelized cost of energy among behind-the-meter technologies), and the Ratepayer Protection Pledge signed by nearly all utilities and several colocation companies is 'a sign of growing support for behind-the-meter power'. Management says the Jenbacher T6 platform (incl. J624) offers industry-leading power density, fast response times and higher rotational inertia for dynamic AI data center loads, with a modular design that accelerates time to power.

items.reason: The CEO sentence is about behind-the-meter solutions.
items.evidence: behind-the-meter solutions are not the bridge solution, but are here to stay
